summary: 1930 L-4 cab lookout on Bunker Hill in the Okanogan NF; 1960 R-6 tower burned in 1973. WillhiteWeb photo captions note footings; site lies in Pasayten Wilderness.

facts.design: 1930 L-4 cab lookout house (gable roof, per WillhiteWeb); 1960 10-foot treated timber R-6 flat tower
facts.status_note: Tower burned in 1973 and structures removed by burning. WillhiteWeb photo captions note footings at the site. No source describes other remains.

access.note: In the Pasayten Wilderness. Listed routes are 26 miles from Billy Goat trailhead via Sand Ridge, or 22 miles via Dean Creek, which is marked closed. Recent fires have made access harder.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands. The Boundary Trail crosses the summit, per WillhiteWeb.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Okanogan National Forest

events.note: L-4 cab lookout house built per the register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb; the Washington lookout list quotes an Aladdin lookout house instead. Materials packed in 25 miles from Billy Goat Corral.
Summer AWS station at the site, activated July 12 and deactivated September 18 (WillhiteWeb); Washington lookout list lists the same dates with Seattle Filter Center
Cabin destroyed by fire in July 1955 while the lookout, Mickey Nickell, was away getting water (Methow Valley News, quoted by the lookout list). Firelookout.com says it accidentally burned in 1955.
Mickey Nickell of Twisp, lookout in 1955
WillhiteWeb: cab accidentally burned, likely in 1958 but no date known. Conflicts with the 1955 date in the other sources.
Chuck Casey named as lookout; WillhiteWeb says lookouts used a wall tent after the cab burned
Lookout replaced with a 10-foot treated timber R-6 flat tower
Gazette-Tribune item: men stationed at Bunker Hill and Monument 83 lookouts that July
WillhiteWeb: the tower was last used in 1966
Tower deliberately burned (firelookout.com); register says burned in 1973
Forest Service removed the structures by burning
Former Fire Lookout Sites registration dated November 10, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register, firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb describe an L-4 cab. A Washington lookout list quotes an Aladdin lookout house for December 1930. The story reports both and does not choose.
The July 1955 newspaper report and firelookout.com put the cab fire in 1955. WillhiteWeb says likely 1958 with no date known. The story gives 1955 and notes WillhiteWeb's date.
firelookout.com says the cab accidentally burned; the 1955 newspaper says the origin was not definitely known. The story uses the newspaper's wording.
firelookout.com lists a lookout named Floyd Boesel in 1929, a year before the 1930 construction date in every other source. The story leaves that name out.

notes_for_editor: The WillhiteWeb page (source 3) was not in the brief's source list; it was found by search and is the only source for the Pasayten Wilderness placement, the 1966 last use and the footing captions. Design and cab-fire date conflict across sources and are reported side by side. The 1929 staffing name in firelookout.com conflicts with the 1930 build, so it is omitted. The brief's status 'gone' and 2012 registration are consistent with the sources. Access is set to public from the route description, with the Dean Creek route marked closed; confirm with the Okanogan-Wenatchee NF before publishing the access line. No photos added.
